insider_note: Compare this to answer 29 right before it: a NEGATIVE leading coefficient under the root (−2x²) is what turns the completed square into a BOUNDED a²−x² shape, which uses Sin⁻¹ rather than the unbounded sinh⁻¹ used in answer 29.

steps.label: Write the multiplier as A·Dr′ + B and solve for A, B
steps.why: The same A·Dr′+B split as answer 29, applied to a quadratic that DECREASES for large x (the −2x² term), which is what gives A a negative value here.
common_mistakes: Missing the minus sign in d/dx(6−2x²+x) = −4x+1, and instead differentiating as if the leading term were +2x².
Sign slip solving A+B=5 for B once A=−3/2 is known.
steps.memory_tip: d/dx(6−2x²+x) = −4x+1 — the minus sign on the x² term carries straight through to the derivative.

steps.label: Substitute back and split the integral
steps.why: The same f′(x)√f(x) power-rule shortcut as answer 29 handles the A-part; the minus sign on A carries through cleanly to give a NEGATIVE leading term this time.
common_mistakes: Losing the negative sign carried from A=−3/2, which makes this term positive instead of negative.
steps.memory_tip: (−3/2)×(2/3) = −1 exactly — the fraction cancels to a clean whole-number coefficient here.

steps.label: Complete the square and apply the standard √(a²−x²) form
steps.why: This time the leading coefficient −2 forces the completed square into an a²−u² shape — a BOUNDED expression under the root — which needs the circular Sin⁻¹ formula, not sinh⁻¹.
common_mistakes: Completing the square into the wrong sign pattern, writing u²−a² (undefined for most x) instead of a²−u².
Confusing Sin⁻¹ with sinh⁻¹ — they are DIFFERENT standard results for opposite sign patterns under the root.
steps.memory_tip: Negative x² coefficient under a root ⇒ bounded a²−u² ⇒ Sin⁻¹ (capital S, circular). Positive ⇒ sinh⁻¹ (small s, hyperbolic), as in answer 29.

steps.label: Combine for the final answer
steps.why: Multiplying B=13/2 into the √2 factor and both terms of the standard √(a²−u²) result, then writing u=x−1/4 as (4x−1)/4 throughout, gives the second and third parts of the answer.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to multiply B=13/2 through BOTH terms of the two-term standard result.
Mixing up a=7/4 with a²=49/16 when substituting into the a²/2 coefficient.
steps.memory_tip: a²/2 = (7/4)²/2 = 49/32 — square a BEFORE halving it, not the other way round.
